# Find footage

`voyager media-search status --json` reports installed tools/models without
installing them. When local indexing is needed, use `media-search setup --kind
speech` or `--kind visual` (or `base` for shared prerequisites). Speech setup
covers Parakeet's 25 European languages; speech in any other language downloads
Whisper turbo (574 MB) once, the first time it is indexed, or ahead of time with
`media-search setup --kind speech --languages all`. Setup downloads
required runtimes/models lazily.

```sh
voyager media index --kind speech --sources '["./interview.wav"]' --json
voyager media index --kind visual --sources '["./demo.mp4"]' --json
```

The index serves search, not transcripts; for word times use `voyager speech
transcribe FILE --local`, which downloads missing speech models itself and waits. Language detection can guess wrong (singing, accents):
both `speech transcribe --local` and `media index --kind speech` take
`--language CODE` (ISO 639) or `--accurate` to override it.

Use `media search` for matching speech or visual content and `media moment` to
inspect a candidate's context. Search prepares missing local evidence and returns
files and source timestamps; wait for its results. Reuse the workspace's index. Large-library retry is an explicit
opt-in via `media-search retry --id ID`. Cancel active preparation with
`media-search cancel --id ID`; do not clear reusable indexes just to recover a
transient failure.

# Compose for social-video interface overlays

Use for YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Instagram/Facebook Reels and Stories.

Default to edge-to-edge video: fill the intended canvas with the picture and keep
subjects large enough to read. Platform controls overlay the video; they are not
margins to subtract from the composition. Do not inset or shrink the whole shot,
add padding, or reserve empty bottom/right bands to satisfy a safe-area guide.

Protect only information the viewer must read or see to understand the beat:
caption words, a necessary label or CTA, a revealing expression, or the exact hand/prop
detail carrying the action. A person's whole body, the entire product and all motion
do not need to fit inside a safe rectangle.
When there is an actual overlap, move or reflow the text, or adjust that shot's framing
locally.
For wide-source adaptations, follow [vertical composition](#build-the-vertical-composition) below.

Move or reflow captions when they cover a face
or action; do not automatically anchor subtitles to the very bottom.

## Automatic check

`voyager media review final.mp4 --platform shorts|tiktok|reels` reads the text on sampled
frames and flags any that sits in these approximate zones, with timestamps and a still that
shows the zones. Pixels are on a 1080×1920 canvas and scale
with the video. The table is generated from `packages/video/src/media/safe-areas.ts`; change
the zones there.

<!-- overlay-zones:start -->
| `--platform` | Top | Bottom | Left | Right | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shorts` (YouTube Shorts) | 288 px (15%) | 672 px (35%) | 48 px (4%) | 192 px (18%) | [Google's universal vertical video-ad safe zone](https://services.google.com/fh/files/misc/universalsafezones-youtube.pdf) |
| `tiktok` (TikTok) | 130 px (7%) | 484 px (25%) | 44 px (4%) | 140 px (13%) | [the conservative end of published in-feed guides; TikTok's own templates vary by caption length](https://ads.tiktok.com/help/article/tiktok-auction-in-feed-ads?lang=en) |
| `reels` (Instagram/Facebook Reels) | 269 px (14%) | 672 px (35%) | 65 px (6%) | 65 px (6%) | [Meta's 9:16 guidance of 14% top, 35% bottom and 6% sides](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/facebook-instagram-reels-ads) |
<!-- overlay-zones:end -->

Text detection uses macOS Vision; elsewhere the check reports `measured: false`. A clean
result covers the sampled frames only, so raise `--samples` (up to 24) for fast-changing captions.

## Build the vertical composition

Use for a new Short or a portrait adaptation.

Do not add a persistent headline or title card simply because the format is a Short.

# Iterative native timeline editing

Use this only when the edit already lives in the video engine's native timeline.
Keep the established editor or FFmpeg path for other work.

Read `voyager capabilities --json` first. Continue only if its video engine is
ready and not off; set `video_bin` below to that engine's `path`.
Check `timeline apply --help` once on the installed engine to discover whether it
supports desired-state apply. Probe and call the same installed binary:

```sh
video_bin="<ready video engine path>"
if "$video_bin" timeline apply --help >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  "$video_bin" -C edit.vvideo timeline snapshot --sequence main --field '' > desired.json
  # Edit sequence in this copied snapshot; preserve stable ids and unrelated contents.
  "$video_bin" -C edit.vvideo timeline apply desired.json --dry-run
  "$video_bin" -C edit.vvideo timeline apply desired.json
fi
```

The snapshot holds `{base_rev, sequence}` from one read. Apply computes the native
diff and commits it as one undo step; unchanged state at the current revision is
a no-op. If another edit made it stale, reread and reconcile the intended change.
Keep existing clip/track ids. Do not clear and rebuild the timeline for a tweak.
If apply is unavailable, use the installed engine's targeted ops in one `apply`
batch for the affected objects and inspect their result.

The whole sequence is authoritative: omitted clips, tracks, captions and
relationships are removed. Start from the snapshot, preserve everything outside
the intended change, and inspect `patches`/`objects` in the dry-run result.
Native title clips are composition clips. Positions/source ranges are absolute;
apply does not ripple or regenerate the supplied captions. Locked changes or
broken references refuse the whole transaction. Removing a parent while keeping
a title or music clip requires keeping that child and clearing or replacing its
attachment in desired state.

For a newly placed title, music bed or overlay that should follow absolute time,
use `--no-auto-attach` on its placement command. In desired state set the clip's
`auto_attach:false` and omit `attach`; explicit `clip attach` can still connect
it later. This avoids a later primary-footage placement creating a connection.
Ordinary magnetic parent deletion retains its existing semantics; use
`clip rm --selection-only` to preserve connected and linked partners.

---
name: edit-video
description: "Find, cut and finish local footage; transcript edits, captions, reframing, grading and audio."
applications:
  - id: ffmpeg
    role: primary
  - id: resolve
    role: alternative
  - id: premiere
    role: alternative
voyager:
  schemaVersion: 1
  design: optional
---

## Cut for what the viewer feels

Left to its defaults, an edit becomes the usable shots in order, trimmed to fit, with
transitions hiding the joins. Refuse that. You are the best editor on this job, and the bar is
a piece people remember. Find the emotional or narrative spine and make every cut earn its
place. In short-form social and ads, hook the viewer in the first 1–3 seconds; a narrative or
slow-burn piece can take its time. Cut on motion, thought or emotion when it carries the viewer
forward. Let a moment breathe when the feeling needs time, and compress what the audience
already understands. Build rhythm through contrast, with sound carrying anticipation and
continuity across the picture. Review the opening, the joins and the whole arc. If a cut only
fills time or a flourish distracts from the moment, push the edit further.

## Route

- DaVinci Resolve or Premiere Pro takes the edit only when the user names one,
  the project already uses it, or they ask for an editable project file in it
  ([davinci-resolve](../davinci-resolve/SKILL.md),
  [premiere-pro](../premiere-pro/SKILL.md)). `voyager capabilities --json`
  says whether its route is ready; not ready, off or unavailable, edit here,
  except when the user named that editor: then name the blocked step and ask
  before cutting here.
  A burned-caption social cut from one recording finishes here unless the user
  names an app or wants an editable timeline.
- For an edit done here, when `<voyager_environment>` lists Voyager's video
  engine as ready, it is the default for cutting and assembling footage, unless
  FFmpeg is the user's named or saved choice; use the bundled FFmpeg for quick
  one-off transforms and when the engine is not ready: [speech edits](#speech-edits)
  for word cuts, replacement lines and captions, and `voyager media assemble` for picture. For H.264 settings, use macOS `-c:v h264_videotoolbox -q:v 85`, Windows `-c:v h264_mf -b:v 12M`, [others](../make-social-loop/references/delivery.md#bundled-ffmpeg-encoders); `drawtext` needs `fontfile=`, `-vsync` is `-fps_mode`, and `-filter_complex_script <file>` is `-/filter_complex <file>`.
- Edit by text: when the user wants to edit a talking recording by its words
  (cut words, clean up fillers, pauses and retakes, fix a word in their voice),
  use `voyager transcript` and show the `voyager.transcript-edit` card
  ([edit by text](#edit-by-text)).
- An audio-only voice recording (cleaning, repairing, levelling, joining or
  comping takes, delivery) is finished as
  [voiceover](../voiceover/SKILL.md#finish-a-recording) describes.
- For CapCut, follow [capcut](../capcut/SKILL.md) for its file handoff;
  for Descript, follow [descript](../descript/SKILL.md) for media import and export.
- For Final Cut Pro, follow [final-cut-pro](../final-cut-pro/SKILL.md).
- An interchange timeline opens in Resolve or Premiere when installed; follow
  the chosen editor's skill for supported formats. Without either app, say in one
  line that it needs one of them. A `.prproj` or `.drp` stays in its app.
- Burned captions: the bundled FFmpeg has no libass (no `subtitles` or `ass`
  filter). Burn them with `drawtext` (or `voyager media assemble`'s timed `text`
  entries), grouped per [caption grouping and timing](#captions); styled or
  kinetic captions, titles, lower thirds, overlays and graphics come from
  [make-motion-graphics](../make-motion-graphics/SKILL.md).
  The video engine's own caption burn (`caption set --burn`,
  `render --burn-captions`) needs Voyager's design engine: when
  `<voyager_environment>` doesn't list it as ready, burn with `drawtext` from the start.

Speaking videos for social get burned-in captions by default, large and readable on a phone; skip them only when the user says so or the format doesn't suit them.

## Start

When the project has a selected brand kit (`brand/manifest.json`, with the kit in
`brand/BRAND.md`), read it as [brand-kit](../brand-kit/SKILL.md) describes
before making titles, captions, lower thirds, cards or graphics, and use its
colours, fonts and logos.

- Word- or line-level speech edits by transcript with FFmpeg (cuts, replacement
  lines, music ducking, synchronized picture timing): [speech edits](#speech-edits).
- Finding lines, shots or moments in a large local library: [find footage](references/find-footage.md).

## Review footage locally

`voyager media review` reports frame timing mismatches and possible flashes at cut and overlay boundaries, with surrounding frame images in `checks.boundaries`.

When choosing takes, dialogue lines or cut points from source footage, reuse
existing transcripts and analysis, then fill gaps for the files relevant to the edit.

Reuse an existing transcript or a voice take's `transcriptPath`;
otherwise `voyager speech transcribe FILE --local --output DIR` writes a
word-timed `DIR/transcript.json` without speaker labels, free on this computer
(a video is transcribed from its first audio track). If the detected language or the words are wrong,
transcribe again into a new `--output` with `--language CODE` (ISO 639-1) or
`--accurate` (Whisper).
Without `--local` it is a paid provider job
([provider shortcuts](#provider-shortcuts)). Read the words and timings before
choosing lines and trimming speech.

For lyric timing or music with sung vocals, use
`voyager speech transcribe FILE --local --no-vad --accurate --language ja --output DIR`
(replace `ja` with the known language, or omit `--language` when unknown).
The speech detector can drop synthetic singing. Structured requests use `vad:false`.
Default local transcription retries once without VAD when it finds no speech in
non-silent audio and reports `retriedWithoutVad:true` with a warning in `warnings`. Check the
words and timings against the supplied lyrics; instrumental music can produce
spurious words.

- Picture and sound: `voyager media review FILE --json` measures loudness,
  silence, black and frozen intervals and returns stills for flagged picture
  checks. Inspect relevant frames around proposed joins for visual continuity.
- Cut points and moments in picture: `voyager media frames FILE --output DIR --around 12.4,31 --json`
  writes one labelled contact sheet (`sheet.jpg`, each frame's time above it)
  and lists each frame's path for a closer look. When the user gives
  timestamps, treat them as correct: one call with every boundary in
  `--around` (seconds, so 1:05.2 is 65.2; up to 12 per call; ±1.5 s every
  0.25 s by default), then read that one sheet and
  set in and out points from it. Sample spread `--times` only for
  moments the user didn't locate; `--crop` reads small
  screen text. Checks such as a private label to mask still happen, from the
  same sheet.

Transcription, media review and frame extraction process footage on this computer without uploading it, so they work under
a no-upload constraint; initial speech setup may download tools and models.
Measurements and sampled frames do not establish delivery, tone or continuous motion.

## Iterative native timeline edits

When the current edit already uses the video engine's native timeline, read
[iterative timeline editing](references/timeline-apply.md) before changing it.
This applies to tweaks of that timeline, including titles and music; keep the
user's chosen editor or FFmpeg workflow for other requests.

The video engine's `check` and edit results flag `audio overlap:` (voices playing over each other, a tail running into the next clip); fix unintended ones before presenting the cut, and leave deliberate layering alone.

## Speech edits

**Several stretches of one file** join in order in one speech-edit recipe,
then one render.

Generated narration: a managed take names its word transcript as `transcriptPath`.
For stock narration, follow [stock narration outputs and timings](../voiceover/SKILL.md#stock-narration).

See [editing routes](../screen-capture/references/editing-routes.md) for shared picture
timing and optional AE import.

### Provider shortcuts

Local transcription disables diarization, and provider `--parameters` do not change
the local engine; it has no speaker-label flag. When the task needs speaker labels,
use Scribe without `--local` and request `diarize:true` as below.

Paid transcription (a video uses its first audio track) and voice isolation:

Before paid transcription, run the same `speech transcribe` request with
`--dry-run --json` and tell the user its `message`: which route runs and which
account pays. Do this before the paid call, including when long audio changes
the route. Fal Scribe accepts files shorter than 20 minutes. For longer Scribe V2
recordings Voyager prefers a connected, enabled ElevenLabs key: one native Scribe
call supports up to 10 hours within Voyager's 512 MiB upload limit and keeps
speaker identities over the full recording. Larger files use chunks.
Studio has no native Scribe route on Voyager credits. Without a native route,
Voyager cuts near silences into chunks below the fal limit, on the previewed
fal/Voyager payer, waits for each durable job and writes a stitched
`transcript.json`. Tell the user that speaker IDs across chunks are best-effort;
matching uses overlap speech and cannot identify a returning speaker absent
from the overlap. `--output NEW_DIR`
chooses the chunked transcript directory.

```sh
voyager speech transcribe ./dialogue.wav --parameters '{"diarize":true}' --dry-run --json
voyager speech transcribe ./dialogue.wav --parameters '{"diarize":true}' --request-id take_transcript --json
voyager speech isolate ./dialogue.wav --request-id take_clean --json
voyager jobs wait JOB_ID --timeout 60 --json
voyager jobs result JOB_ID --json
```

Defaults are
ElevenLabs Scribe V2 and audio isolation. `--model` selects a compatible
endpoint and `--parameters` supplies native options; generic `media generate`
remains available for other shapes. Exact request-ID retries do not buy another job.

New narration and changed lines of generated narration are managed voice work: follow
[voiceover](../voiceover/SKILL.md) for casting, pronunciation, takes and
repairs. Words in a person's own recording are fixed in their voice with
`voyager transcript replace` ([edit by text](#edit-by-text)), never a cast voice. `voyager
speech narrate` (Eleven v4 directly through Voyager, e.g. `--voice Sarah`) remains a
separate route for when the user explicitly chooses it, and is never a substitute when managed voice is
unavailable. A voice take's audio (`audioAbsolutePath`) and word transcript
(`transcriptPath`) plug into the edit plan below as a source or replacement.

`normalize AUDIO --response PROVIDER_JSON --model ENDPOINT --output NEW_DIR
--json` retains raw JSON and creates `transcript.json` with stable occurrence
IDs, speakers, source hash and word times. It accepts Scribe-style `words` with
text/start/end in seconds.
For capture audio, include `--source-start-us` from the track and
`--timeline-duration-us` from `capture.json`.

### Local edit plan

Write an edit recipe; retained segments run in listed order:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "picture": "follow",
  "crossfadeMs": 8,
  "segments": [
    { "id": "intro", "selection": { "startUs": 0, "endUs": 2000000 } },
    {
      "id": "line",
      "selection": { "startUs": 4000000, "endUs": 6000000 },
      "replacement": { "path": "replacement.wav", "fit": "natural" },
      "caption": "Open the export menu.",
      "facecam": "hide"
    }
  ]
}
```

```sh
voyager speech plan --transcript ./transcript/transcript.json --edits ./edits.json --output ./speech-plan --json
voyager speech render ./speech-plan/plan.json --output ./speech-render --json
```

Or use `speech plan AUDIO --edits ...` without transcription. Word selections use
`firstWord`/`lastWord` IDs, optional `leadUs`/`trailUs`.
Selection times are integer microseconds on the source timeline.

`picture: "follow"` shares cuts/rates with picture, cursor, camera and captions.
`"locked"` keeps the whole original picture timeline; segments must cover it
unchanged. Replacement `fit: "natural"` uses its measured duration; `pad` adds
silence to a longer explicit span; `stretch` explicitly changes speech rate
while preserving pitch. Set `outputDurationUs` when needed.

Optional recipe `audio:{path,offsetUs}` uses cleaned dialogue while preserving
original timing. `music:{path,gainDB,duck}` adds a
bed, and `loudnessLUFS` opts into normalization. `speech analyze AUDIO --json`
measures silence, loudness and peaks without editing. Crossfade defaults to 8 ms;
zero disables it. Render writes WAV, SRT/VTT, measurements and a durable `render.json`.

For a capture composition, add `speech:{path:"./speech-render/render.json"}` to
its AE recipe; it adopts the speech timeline and replaces the corresponding
original audio layer. Optional `captions:false` omits text layers. `animationTime:
"source"` also moves authored zoom/facecam keys through the edit.

For designed or kinetic caption treatments, pass the timed words to
[make-motion-graphics](../make-motion-graphics/SKILL.md).

## Edit by text

Available when the user wants to edit talking footage by its words. The recording
comes from the Record panel or `voyager capture` (macOS), or any imported file.

- `voyager transcript open --media FILE --json` makes `<name>.vvideo` in the
  workspace and transcribes it on this computer, with speakers. Every command
  prints the card model (words with ids, removed and voiced words, retake groups).
- Show the card with `show_widget` `{source:{kind:"definition",id:"voyager.transcript-edit"}, inputs:{project:"/abs/<name>.vvideo"}}`;
  it loads the model itself and stays current as you edit. Shown while `open` is still
  transcribing, it says so and opens when the transcript is ready. Don't edit or
  promote a revision of this card: a changed card can't play the project's media.
- Edits: `cut --words w0012..w0020`, `restore --words …|--reason filler|--all`,
  `clean` (fillers, pauses over `--max-ms`, retakes; or any one flag), `take --id t1 --keep N`,
  `replace --words w1..w2 --text "…"` (the speaker's voice; picture holds), `undo`, `redo`,
  `export` (MP4 and SRT beside the project). All take `--project P --json`.
- Each change renders a draft preview in the background; `export` and the next change
  stop it themselves. To stop one that competes with other work, run `preview --stop`: it
  answers once every process the render started has exited. A `note` instead means it had
  already ended or couldn't be stopped safely; leave its processes alone. Never stop it with
  `voyager video job cancel`, which can leave its sound mix running.
- Suggested retakes (`applied:false`) are the user's call in the card; keep one only
  when the user asks you to choose.
- A fix in the speaker's voice uses their saved clone, or a one-off copy
  only after the user ticks consent in the card; you can't give that consent.
  The copy's model (hosted or on this computer) is the user's choice in
  Settings → Creative preferences → Voice fixes.
- `replace` is for a person's own recording. For generated narration,
  regenerate the line ([voiceover](../voiceover/SKILL.md)).
- The cut is rebuilt on every change, in the sequence `show` names (`edit`, or
  `edit-by-text` if the project already had `edit`). Direct edits to it are refused
  (CUT_EDITED_ELSEWHERE): `sequence dup` it first to keep them.
- `changed.warnings` lists cuts the engine thinks may clip a word; listen to
  those joins before calling the edit done.

## Captions

The speech render's SRT/VTT already groups words: it breaks on a 500 ms pause or
a sentence end, up to 3 s and 48 characters per cue, with cue times at the
words. Use those for sidecar files.

For Shorts, TikTok, Reels or Stories, use [interface-safe composition](references/social-safe-areas.md) when placing captions.
